title: The camera that follows you
summary: The view in R.E.P.O. is placed by a component of its own: it holds the player's transform, an offset in all three axes, the camera controller it drives and a smoothing value.
body: The camera is not welded to the player. There is a component whose job is to position the camera, which is why the view can lag and settle rather than moving as one rigid piece with the body.
It works from the player's own transform. The component holds the transform it follows, so what it tracks is the player rather than a point in the level.
The offset is in three axes. There is a separate offset for each axis, which is why a view can sit above and behind a player without being a single distance in front of them.
It drives a camera controller. The component refers to the camera controller it moves, so the same controller can be used for more than one way of positioning a view.
It smooths the result. There is a value for smoothing the position, which is why the camera catches up rather than snapping when a player turns or is thrown.
What this entry does not tell you: what the offset is set to, how much smoothing is applied, or how many cameras a run uses. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: A component of its own positions the camera.
It follows the player's own transform, with an offset in each of the three axes.
It drives a camera controller and smooths the position it arrives at.
The camera has named movements of its own: a bob, a shake and a zoom, with separate positions for crouching and crawling.
facts.evidence: asset names: CameraBob, CameraShake, CameraZoom, CameraCrouchPosition, CameraCrawlPosition
